author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: For AlliedWare Plus switches and AR-series UTM and VPN firewalls. Add the data collector with log host <address> and a filter, such as log host <address> level informational: firewall logs are local5.info, commands user.notice, and URL filtering and antivirus warnings. Add log to the firewall rules to log, run connection-log events all for connection logs, and set log date-format iso so the time carries the year and offset; the default BSD time has neither and is read as UTC. Firewall rule, default deny, probe, invalid and flood lines and connection logs go to Netflow: DENY and REJECT as blocked, PERMIT and connections as allowed, LOG left unset, with the MACs, a connection's packet and byte counts, and the NAT address and port its reply shows. The rule, action, reason, interfaces, TCP flags, ICMP type and code and DPI mark go to event_metadata. URL filtering (Web_Control) goes to HTTP with the URL, requester, action, categories and rule. Antivirus detections go to Antivirus as blocked file threats, with the requesting host in event_metadata. Commands (IMISH, [user@terminal]command) go to Management Event with the user, command and terminal. IPS alerts aren't covered: Allied Telesis doesn't document their text. Login and sshd lines are left to the built-in Login_Master and Sshd_Master parsers, which claim them. Older releases log commands without [user@terminal]; those aren't claimed. How sure this is: the message bodies come from Allied Telesis's Firewall and NAT guide and Log Message Reference. The on-wire header (<PRI><time> <host> <program>[<pid>]:) is inferred from the logging guide's message format, and the program that writes connection logs isn't documented, so the parser reads them from any program. Samples are made up in the documented shapes. Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-16 (147 of 147 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there. Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (147 of 147 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs). No built-in parser competed for the lines this entry claims. An ICMP error repeats the packet it answers in brackets, and the split keeps the last copy of a key, so the parent takes the bracketed packet out first: the fields are the outer packet's.
